app.unitsImperialDetail: lb, mi, ft and in, °F, fl oz
app.checkForUpdatesHint: Once a day Pulse asks GitHub whether a newer version is out. Nothing about you is sent.

profile.title: Profile
profile.photoStays: Your photo stays on this phone
profile.daysStart: Your days start at midnight in your time zone. Edit changes it and recomputes your scores.
profile.cameraDenied: Allow the camera in Android settings to take a photo.

delete.title: Delete everything?
delete.description: Removes everything Pulse stored on this phone: imported data, scores, journal, logs, profile and settings. Health Connect keeps its own copy. Export what you want to keep first (More › Your data).
delete.descriptionFinal: This can’t be undone: your data is only on this phone, so nothing can bring it back. Pulse asks for your profile again.

source.sampleBody: Every screen runs on generated data. Connect Health Connect to score your own Fitbit data.
source.notConnectedBody: Connect Health Connect, where the Google Health app writes your Fitbit data. Pulse only reads it; nothing leaves your phone.
source.revokedBody: Health Connect access was removed. Sync is paused until you allow it again.
source.updateBody: Health Connect needs an update. Update it from the Play Store, then sync again.
source.unavailableBody: Health Connect isn’t available on this phone.
source.checkFailed: Couldn’t run the data check. Try again.
source.noFitbitBody: With “Fitbit only”, Pulse found no records from the Google Health app that weren’t measured by the phone. Either Google Health isn’t sharing with Health Connect yet, or it labels its records as the phone’s. “Fitbit first” uses the phone’s data on days the Fitbit has none.
source.skippedBody: Health Connect refused a few {{types}} records because the app that wrote them saved times that don’t add up, such as an end before the start. Pulse left those out and imported the rest. Fixing or deleting them in that app brings them in on the next sync.
source.morePermissionsBody: Allow every data type, including past data, so Pulse can read all of what your Fitbit writes. Sync keeps working until then.
source.dataCheckHint: Compares the last 10 days in Health Connect, app by app, with what Pulse stored. Shares the report.
source.reimportBody: Pulse reads the last 180 days from Health Connect again and rescores them, for data an app shared late. Your journal and profile stay.
source.sampleConfirmBody: Pulse removes what it imported from Health Connect and fills every screen with 180 days of generated data. Your profile is kept for when you switch back.
source.sampleFailed: Couldn’t build the sample data. Try again.

bg.allowToast: Allow background access so Pulse can read Health Connect while closed
bg.title: Background sync
bg.syncHint: Imports Health Connect and rescores while Pulse is closed.
bg.needsHc: Needs Health Connect as the data source.
bg.androidDecides: Android decides when it runs: every 15 minutes at best, often hours apart when you rarely open Pulse or Battery Saver is on. Pulse always syncs when you open it.
bg.restricted: Background tasks are restricted for Pulse on this phone.
bg.accessHint: Health Connect only answers a closed app with this permission.
bg.batteryOk: Pulse may run in the background, so a sync finishes.
bg.batteryHint: Many phones pause Pulse a few seconds into a background sync, which then stalls. Under Battery, choose Allow background activity or Unrestricted.

notif.title: Notifications
notif.blocked: Notifications are blocked in Android settings. Allow them for Pulse there, then come back.
notif.blockedToast: Notifications are blocked. Allow them for Pulse in Android settings.
notif.recoveryReadyHint: Once a day, when today’s Recovery is scored.
notif.cantSyncHint: Once a day, when Health Connect hasn’t synced for 36 hours.
notif.strainTargetHint: Once a day, when Day Strain reaches today’s target.
notif.healthMonitorHint: When last night’s vitals leave your normal range or an illness signal appears; not again while it lasts.
notif.weeklyReportHint: Monday morning, when last week’s report is ready.
notif.checkInHint: Every day at the time below; opens the Journal.
notif.windDownDefault: Before tonight’s planned bedtime, from the sleep planner.
notif.footer: Alerts are checked after every sync, in the background or when Pulse opens. Nothing leaves the phone.

live.title: Live heart rate
live.autoConnectHint: Off by default to save the band’s battery. On: Pulse connects whenever it opens and the band is sharing.
live.forgetBody: Pulse disconnects and stops reconnecting to it. Search again to pick a band.
live.nearbyNote: Android asks for Nearby devices (scan and connect) only. Pulse never uses your location for this.
live.quickSettings: Turn Bluetooth on from Quick Settings.
live.quickSettingsBack: Turn Bluetooth on from Quick Settings, then come back.
live.step1Body: In Google Health, open your Fitbit Air › Connections and turn on Share heart rate.
live.step2Body: Turn it on so the band keeps sharing outside workouts. It uses more of the band’s battery.
live.step3Body: Come back to Pulse: it looks for the band. Tap it in the list to connect.
live.googleHealthFailed: Couldn’t open Google Health. Open it from your home screen.
live.noBluetoothBody: This phone (or emulator) has no Bluetooth Low Energy, so live heart rate can’t work on it.
live.bluetoothUnavailableBody: This build of Pulse can’t use Bluetooth.
live.bluetoothOffBody: Turn it on to find your band.
live.nearbyBlockedBody: Nearby devices is off for Pulse. Allow it in Android settings › Apps › Pulse › Permissions.
live.nearbyBody: Pulse needs it to find and connect to your band. It doesn’t use your location.
live.lookingFor: Looking for bands sharing heart rate…
live.goLiveIntro: Beat by beat from your band, over Bluetooth.
live.batteryNote: Sharing uses the band’s battery, and the band takes one connection at a time: while Pulse holds it, gym equipment or another app can’t connect. Pulse lets go {{seconds}} seconds after you leave it and reconnects when you come back.
live.viewingNote: Live readings are for viewing; scores use what Pulse reads from Health Connect.
